input: Negotiate a raise at my annual review

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The timeline to the review determines how much preparation time is available and shapes the urgency of each step.
Industry, company size, and role level heavily influence what raise percentage is realistic and what arguments will land best.
Knowing the current salary and target amount defines whether this is a modest cost-of-living ask or a significant jump, which changes the strategy entirely.
The relationship with and style of the decision-maker (direct manager, HR, skip-level) affects tone, framing, and how to handle pushback.
Understanding what 'winning' looks like — a specific number, a minimum floor, or openness to non-salary perks — determines when to hold firm vs. accept a deal.
The user's comfort with direct negotiation vs. collaborative framing affects which scripts, tactics, and rehearsal methods to recommend.
Whether the user needs help gathering evidence, scripting the conversation, doing mock negotiation practice, or all three determines the immediate first action.

gold.taskTitle: Negotiate a raise at my annual review
gold.taskDescription: Prepare for and successfully negotiate a salary increase during an upcoming annual performance review.

questions.title: When exactly is your annual review scheduled?
questions.description: Establish the date of the review to determine how much preparation time is available and set the pacing of each step.

questions.title: What is your industry, role level, and company size?
questions.description: Understand the professional context to benchmark a realistic raise target and tailor the negotiation strategy accordingly.

questions.title: What is your current salary and the raise amount you are targeting?
questions.description: Define the starting point and goal so the plan addresses the right scale of negotiation — incremental adjustment vs. a significant jump.

questions.title: Who will be making the final decision on your raise?
questions.description: Identify whether the decision-maker is a direct manager, HR, or a senior leader, as this shapes how to frame arguments and handle the conversation.

questions.title: What is your absolute minimum acceptable outcome from this review?
questions.description: Clarify the floor — a specific number, a promotion title, or non-salary benefits — so the plan includes clear walk-away and trade-off criteria.

questions.title: Do you prefer a direct ask or a more collaborative, data-led approach?
questions.description: Understand the user's natural negotiation style and comfort level to recommend scripts and tactics that feel authentic rather than forced.

questions.title: What do you most need help with — research, scripting, or practice?
questions.description: Pinpoint the immediate next action so the plan starts with the highest-leverage deliverable for the user right now.
